small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs sweeping BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_OC=256 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4, and try BLOCK_OC=32 with BLOCK_N=256 — OC=64 means BLOCK_OC=128 wastes half the tile, and a tighter OC tile may actually win.
- Swap the program-id ordering (pid_oc on axis 0, pid_n on axis 1) and/or add an L2-friendly swizzle (group rows of pid_n) to improve weight reuse across pid_n tiles since the weight tensor is small (64·8·9 = ~18KB) and should stay resident.
- The IC_PAD=16 pad doubles K work (IC=8 real). Consider doing two kw positions per dot (concat along K to get K=16 of real data) so the tl.dot fills its K dim with useful FLOPs instead of zero-padding.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM where K = IC*KH*KW = 72 is fully contracted in one tl.dot per tile (BLOCK_K=72 padded to 80/96). With KH=KW=3 and IC=8, the entire K dimension fits in registers; eliminate the static kh/kw loop and do a single dot per output tile, dramatically improving MAC density.
- Switch to a channels-last (NHWC) layout for x and out so the IC axis is the contiguous one, enabling vectorized coalesced loads along the GEMM-K dimension; transpose weights once at init to (KH,KW,IC,OC) layout.
- Consider a persistent-CTA design: with N_OUT=128·126·126≈2M and OC=64, grid is huge; a persistent kernel that loops over output tiles keeps weights cached in shared memory / registers across tiles and amortizes weight loads.
